ops_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the creation of our team chat workspace using {{vendor}}. Before starting, ask me for: (1) our company/team name to use as the workspace name, (2) the primary domain or work email domain that should be associated with the workspace, (3) an initial list of channels we want (e.g., #general, #random, #eng, #sales), noting which should be public vs private and who should have membership, and (4) any integrations we already know we want from an app directory/marketplace (e.g., calendar, CRM, docs tools), plus any custom slash commands or incoming webhook use cases we anticipate needing.

Using my answers, please draft a complete setup plan: a proposed workspace name, the full channel list with public/private designations and suggested initial members per channel, a shortlist of marketplace integrations to install with a one-line rationale for each, and a description (in words, no endpoints) of any custom slash commands or incoming webhook message flows we'd want to configure. Also prepare a checklist of the exact steps a workspace owner/admin will need to click through in {{vendor}}'s workspace-creation flow (team name entry, domain verification, channel creation, integration installs) using our configured credentials.

Do not attempt to create the workspace, verify the domain, accept any terms of service, or finalize billing — creating the org-level workspace and confirming domain ownership/billing remains a human step that only our workspace owner/admin can complete. Compile your draft plan and checklist into a single summary document and then stop for human sign-off before any workspace is actually provisioned.

ops_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me set up default channels in our {{vendor}} team-chat workspace as part of onboarding. Before making any changes, ask me for: (1) the workspace/domain to use, (2) the list of default channel names I want (e.g., #general, #announcements, #random, #eng, #ops), (3) for each channel whether it should be public or private, and (4) a short topic/description for each channel. If I haven't given you these, propose a sensible default set based on common team-chat conventions and ask me to confirm or edit it.

Once I confirm the channel list, visibility settings, and topics, prepare the exact set of actions you will run using the {{vendor}} CLI, one per channel, in this form: `{{vendor}} channels create --name "channel-name" --type stream --visibility open` (use `--visibility private` where I specified private), along with the topic text you will set on each channel afterward. Present this full plan — channel names, visibility, and topics — as a clear checklist for my review.

Do not create, modify, or apply any channels or topics yet. This step requires my explicit approval before any changes are applied, so after presenting the checklist, stop for human sign-off. Once I explicitly approve, execute the approved commands using my configured credentials, then report back confirming which channels were created, their visibility settings, and the topics applied, plus any errors or channels that already existed.

ops_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me invite team members to our {{vendor}} team chat workspace as part of setting up team chat. Before taking action, ask me for anything you need that isn't already provided: (1) confirmation that {{vendor}} is the vendor we're using and that the workspace already exists, (2) the list of team members to invite (names, email addresses, and intended roles such as admin or member), (3) which channels (public or private) each person should be added to, and (4) whether we're using {{vendor}}'s API/admin console with my configured credentials or the standard web dashboard.

Once you have this information, prepare a complete invite plan: a table listing each person's email, assigned role, and target channel memberships (noting which channels are private vs public and who should have access). If {{vendor}} supports it, draft the actual invite payload or the sequence of dashboard/API actions you would take to send the invitations and add each person to the correct channels, but do NOT send any invites, create memberships, or make any changes yet.

Because approval is required before changes are applied, present the full invite plan and draft actions to me for review and then stop for human sign-off. Do not invite anyone, modify channel membership, or submit any requests to {{vendor}} until I explicitly approve.

When you report back, include: the finalized invite list with roles and channel assignments, the exact steps or API calls (described in words, not raw endpoints) you're ready to execute, and a clear note that you are awaiting my approval before proceeding.

ops_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me configure notification defaults for our {{vendor}} team chat workspace, which we've already set up with channels and integrations. Notification sprawl leads to alert fatigue, so the goal is to establish sane workspace-wide and channel-level defaults so only meaningful activity interrupts people.

Before starting, ask me for:
1. My {{vendor}} workspace domain/URL (if not already known from prior setup steps).
2. Confirmation of which channels exist and their purpose (e.g., #general, #incidents, #random) if you don't already have this from the channel-setup step.
3. Any specific keywords I want flagged workspace-wide (e.g., company name, product name, "urgent", "outage").
4. Our team's working hours / timezone, so you can set a reasonable quiet-hours or do-not-disturb schedule.

Using your configured credentials, log into the workspace admin settings and:
- Set workspace-level default notification preferences (e.g., mentions and direct messages notify immediately; general channel activity does not).
- For high-traffic or low-priority channels, configure muted or digest-style defaults; for critical channels (incidents, alerts), configure immediate notification defaults.
- Set up keyword-based notification triggers for the terms I provide.
- Configure a default quiet-hours/do-not-disturb schedule aligned with our working hours, if the platform supports scheduling.
- Document any per-channel overrides you make and why.

Done looks like: workspace defaults are configured so mentions/DMs always notify, noisy channels are muted or digest-only by default, critical channels notify immediately, keyword alerts are active, and a quiet-hours schedule is in place — all without needing individual users to manually adjust settings on day one.

Report back with a summary table of channel names, their notification default (immediate/mute/digest), any keyword triggers configured, and the quiet-hours schedule applied, plus any channels where you couldn't set a default and why.
